newsitem.title: UK: UK securities firm Philip Alexander stops business.
newsitem.headline: UK securities firm Philip Alexander stops business.

text.p: British financial markets watchdog the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) said on Wednesday that Philip Alexander Securities and Futures Ltd had agreed to cease investment business.

The SFA said in a statement that an administration order under the Insolvency Act of 1986 had been made relating to the firm in the High Court last week. It said that in making the order the court had been satisfied the firm is, or is likely to become unable to pay its debts.
"In these circumstances SFA is not satisfied that the firm is financially sound or that it has sufficient financial resources to comply with SFA's rules," it added.

As a result the firm had agreed to "cease forthwith from carrying on any investment business for which authorisation under the Financial Services Act is required". It had also agreed not to dispose or deal with any assets without SFA's prior approval.

The firm, which was authorised to conduct investment business under its previous name First Futures Brokers Ltd in April 1988, also agreed to transfer control of remaining client money balances to the administrators.

The SFA said that in April 1995 it had issued a press release stating that during 1994 it had identified "several areas of concern relating to the manner in which (it) conducted business introduced to it by unregulated overseas introducing brokers".
Concerns included poor performance of client accounts, excessive commission and charges and the large number and similarity of complaints.
By April 1995 these problems had not been resolved to the SFA's satisfaction and the firm agreed not to accept new clients introduced to it by unregulated overseas brokers.
